tasks.short: Set up and monitor treatment equipment, check it works, record treatment and settings, write the progress note, save it to the dossier, and tell the therapist how the patient responded.

steps.what: Physical therapist assistant monitors operation of equipment during treatment
Physical therapist assistant checks equipment works and reports faults
Physical therapist assistant records use of equipment and administration of treatment in the paper log
Physical therapist assistant writes the progress note for the therapist
Physical therapist assistant files the note in the patient folder
Physical therapist assistant tells the therapist how the patient responded

tasks.design: Treatment and equipment settings are recorded in a structured form in the practice system ({OTHER}) with pick lists, instead of a paper log. After the session the assistant dictates a few sentences; a bounded step turns them into the SOEP fields, settings come from the form by code, and once the assistant has reviewed every field the note is saved to the dossier, where it stays under the therapist's responsibility. Monitoring equipment and reporting to the therapist stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatments were logged on paper and notes typed after the session.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems take structured treatment records and drafted notes.
tasks.still_hard: Busy days push notes to the end of the day.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a patient tire before the machine shows it.

reach.learn: Whether notes reach the dossier the same day.

evidence.claim: Fysio.AI in Intramed records the physiotherapy intake and writes a structured report into the intake form; the therapist checks and corrects it.
The therapist keeps a dossier with the health data needed for good care for 20 years.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment plan to the therapist informed; changing the plan is outside.
Input contract: treatment plan from the therapist; pick lists set by the practice; fallback is paper and typing.
Monitoring and reporting do not change.
Only the assistant's dictation is recorded, not the treatment session.

research_questions: How long does reviewing a drafted note take?

already_counted.description: Physical therapist assistant reviews each drafted note.

incremental.description: Physical therapist assistant dictates the note after each session.

approvals.approved_version: The progress note as reviewed by the assistant in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short sessions with little to record; high: many treatments with equipment settings per day.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose courses, register, attend continuing education and in-service sessions, read course materials, prepare and give an in-service session, and keep the record of courses and points.

steps.what: Physical therapist assistant chooses continuing education courses and seminars
Physical therapist assistant registers for the chosen courses online
Physical therapist assistant attends continuing education courses, seminars or in-service activities
Physical therapist assistant reads course materials
Physical therapist assistant prepares and conducts an in-service session for colleagues
Physical therapist assistant keeps the record of courses and points on paper

tasks.design: Completed courses and points are recorded in the practice's training overview ({LMS}), where course providers' certificates are uploaded once. In-service sessions use slides kept in a shared practice library ({DOCS}), so earlier sessions are reused. Choosing, registering, attending and teaching colleagues stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Courses and points were tracked on paper and in-service slides rebuilt each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Training overviews record courses and certificates; shared libraries hold slides.
tasks.still_hard: Time for courses competes with patient hours.
tasks.human_edge: Showing colleagues a new breathing technique hands-on.

evidence.claim: Training overviews can record completed courses and certificates per staff member.

assumptions: Boundary: from course offers to the course record; the practice's training budget is outside.
Input contract: certificates from course providers; fallback is paper records.
Attending and teaching do not change.
Course fees are approved as today.

approvals.approved_version: The courses as chosen by the assistant in s1.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one course a year; high: frequent in-service sessions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the therapist's plan, perform postural drainage, percussion or vibration, teach deep breathing exercises, choose home exercises, give them to the patient, and record the treatment.

steps.what: Physical therapist assistant reads the therapist's treatment plan
Physical therapist assistant performs postural drainage, percussions or vibrations to treat respiratory conditions
Physical therapist assistant teaches deep breathing exercises
Physical therapist assistant chooses home exercises for the patient
Physical therapist assistant prints and hands over the exercise sheet
Physical therapist assistant records the treatment

tasks.design: Home breathing exercises come from the practice's exercise library with short videos; once the assistant has chosen them, they go to the patient's app instead of a printed sheet. The treatment is recorded with pick lists in the practice system ({OTHER}). Airway clearance and teaching breathing stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercise sheets were printed and treatments written up in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient apps carry exercise videos from practice libraries.
tasks.still_hard: Breathing technique is learned by feel, not from a video.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a breathless patient enough to start the exercise.

reach.learn: Whether patients practise more with videos.

evidence.claim: Practice systems offer patient apps with appointment messages; exercise libraries with videos can be sent to patients.

assumptions: Boundary: from the treatment plan to the treatment noted; changing the plan is outside.
Input contract: exercise library kept by the practice therapists; fallback is printed sheets.
Patients watch the video in about the time they read the sheet; no added patient time.
Treatment and teaching do not change.
research_questions: Do patients practise more at home?

incremental.description: Physical therapist assistant helps patients open the app.

approvals.approved_version: The home exercises as chosen by the assistant in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly in-practice treatment; high: many patients with home programmes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count supplies, decide and place orders, answer the phone and book appointments, take messages for therapists, fill out insurance and referral forms, and send claims.

steps.what: Physical therapist assistant takes inventory of supplies on the shelves
Physical therapist assistant decides which supplies to order
Physical therapist assistant orders supplies in the supplier's web shop
Patients phone the practice to book or change appointments
Physical therapist assistant answers the telephone and books appointments
Physical therapist assistant takes messages for therapists on paper notes
Physical therapist assistant fills out insurance and referral forms
Physical therapist assistant sends claims to insurers

tasks.design: Supplies get reorder points on the shelves and a standing order in the supplier's web shop, so only low items are counted; once the assistant has decided, the order goes out. Patients book and change routine appointments online and get reminders from the practice system ({OTHER}), and phone messages for therapists go into its task list. Forms and claims are filled from the treatment record; once the assistant has completed them, claims go to insurers through the claims channel after a built-in check. Talking with patients who call stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shelves were counted, every booking came by phone and messages were paper notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems offer online booking, reminders, task lists and checked claims.
tasks.still_hard: Older patients keep phoning to book.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing on the phone that a patient is in more pain than they say.
tasks.altitude: The assistant handles exceptions instead of routine bookings and counts.

reach.learn: Whether messages get answered the same day.

evidence.claim: Intramed sends appointment confirmations and reminders to patients and sends claims to insurers via VECOZO after a built-in check.
Health data in appointments and claims are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from supply shelves and patient calls to claims sent; payment by insurers is outside.
Input contract: treatment records by therapists; supplier web shop; fallback is phone, paper and typing.
Patients who book online spend about the same time as on the phone; priced as customer time.
Clinical questions in messages go to the therapist unanswered by the system.

incremental.description: Physical therapist assistant works the claims rejection list.
Patients book and change appointments online.

approvals.approved_version: The order as decided by the assistant in s2.
The claims as completed by the assistant in s7.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older patients who phone; high: most bookings online and claims from the record.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The physical therapist assistant keeps treating, teaching exercises, watching patients and talking with them; paper logs, typed notes, booking calls and hand-filled forms shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An assistant with more time for patients during treatment.
